catalog.label: Services exported
catalog.note: Commercial services sold abroad - transport, travel, IT, business services. Balance-of-payments data, a different measurement basis from the customs records behind every goods figure on this site. Never add the two.

catalog.label: Services imported
catalog.note: Commercial services bought from abroad, on the same balance-of-payments basis as services exports.

catalog.label: Foreign investment in
catalog.note: Direct investment flowing into the economy, net of disinvestment. A capital flow, not trade: it can be negative when foreign investors withdraw more than they put in.

catalog.label: Foreign investment out
catalog.note: Direct investment this economy's residents made abroad, net of withdrawals.

catalog.label: Remittances received
catalog.note: Money sent home by residents working abroad, plus compensation of employees. For several economies this is larger than any single export sector and appears nowhere in customs data.

catalog.label: Remittances sent
catalog.note: Money sent abroad by foreign workers resident in this economy.

catalog.label: Shipping connectivity
catalog.note: UNCTAD's Liner Shipping Connectivity Index: how well the country is plugged into container shipping networks, scaled so the 2004 maximum is 100. An index of network position, NOT a freight rate - corridor-level rates are commercial data this project does not license.

catalog.label: Container port traffic
catalog.note: Twenty-foot equivalent units moved through the country's ports, including transshipment - which is why the hubs (Singapore, UAE) sit far above what their own trade would suggest.

catalog.label: Lead time to export
catalog.note: Median days from the port of loading to the destination port. Survey-based, and the series stops in 2018 - it is a structural picture, not a current one.

catalog.label: Lead time to import
catalog.note: Median days from the origin port to the port of discharge. Same survey and same 2018 frontier as the export series.

catalog.label: Customs efficiency
catalog.note: How efficient border clearance is, scored 1-5 by freight forwarders who actually cross it. The closest public proxy for non-tariff friction, and a perception score - it counts nobody's certificates, quotas or standards.

catalog.label: Logistics performance
catalog.note: The Logistics Performance Index overall score, 1-5: customs, infrastructure, shipment pricing, service quality, tracking and timeliness combined.

catalog.label: Trade infrastructure
catalog.note: Quality of ports, roads, rail and IT for trade, scored 1-5.

catalog.label: Delivery timeliness
catalog.note: How often shipments reach the consignee within the scheduled time, 1-5.

catalog.label: Rule of law
catalog.note: Worldwide Governance Indicators estimate, roughly -2.5 to +2.5: confidence in contract enforcement, property rights, the police and the courts. A composite of many underlying sources, each with its own error.

catalog.label: Government effectiveness
catalog.note: Perceived quality of public services and policy implementation, -2.5 to +2.5.

catalog.label: Regulatory quality
catalog.note: Perceived ability to formulate rules that permit private-sector development, -2.5 to +2.5.

catalog.label: Control of corruption
catalog.note: Perceived extent to which public power is used for private gain, -2.5 to +2.5. Higher is cleaner.

catalog.label: GDP deflator
catalog.note: The economy's own price level, indexed to a base year that DIFFERS BY COUNTRY. Usable to deflate one country's series over time; not comparable between countries as a level.

catalog.label: Consumer inflation
catalog.note: Annual change in consumer prices. Every trade figure on this site is nominal USD, so a rising series is part growth and part price.

catalog.label: Exchange rate
catalog.note: Local currency units per US dollar, annual average. Trade reported in local currency passes through this before it becomes a USD figure.

catalog.label: Real GDP growth
catalog.note: Annual growth in constant local currency - the real-terms benchmark to read a nominal trade change against.

services.label: Services trade
services.blurb: Commercial services bought and sold across borders. Balance-of-payments data, not customs records, and invisible in every goods figure here.

finance.label: Money that is not trade
finance.blurb: Investment and remittance flows. These move money across the same borders as the goods do, and for some economies they move more of it.

connectivity.label: Getting goods there
connectivity.blurb: Network position, port throughput and how long a shipment actually takes. Public indices only - corridor freight rates are commercial data.

logistics.label: Friction at the border
logistics.blurb: Survey scores for customs, infrastructure and reliability. The closest public read on the barriers a tariff schedule does not describe.

governance.label: Institutions
governance.blurb: Composite governance estimates. Slow-moving, heavily caveated, and the context in which a contract either is or is not enforceable.

prices.label: Prices and currency
prices.blurb: Inflation, the deflator and the exchange rate. Every figure on this site is nominal USD, so these are what separate growth from price.
